summary: In this excerpt from Book 6 (part 55) of a fiction series, the narrator, who is armed with a Colt .45-type pistol, is confronted by a female federal agent who asks him to freeze and drop his weapon. The narrator has just fought in a scene where people were killed, and the agent says his actions were a sensational disruption of her investigation, though she seems to accept self-defense. A male partner then arrives behind him, orders him to surrender, and accidentally steps on something that is a bomb. The narrator warns the building will explode in under five minutes, and the agents accuse him of rigging it, which he denies.
one_line: A narrator is held at gunpoint by a federal agent and her partner in a rigged building that is about to explode.
key_facts: The narrator is holding a Nineteen-eleven pistol, which the female agent identifies as a .45.
The agent says she just came from a scene where twelve people were killed with a .45.
The narrator notes that technically only seven of the twelve were killed with the gun, and the other five were napalmed.
The agent says the narrator's work looked like self-defense but was also a sensational disruption of an active investigation.
The narrator's left hand goes stiff and numb while he holds the gun in a two-handed stance.
A male voice behind the narrator orders him to put his weapon down and place his hands on his head.
The male agent steps on something that makes a click, which the narrator recognizes as a bomb trigger.
The narrator says the place is going up in just under five minutes.
The female agent threatens to riddle the narrator with holes if he does not drop his weapon.
The narrator insists the bomb is not his and that it was rigged before he arrived.
